wu: Warm-up: 'Celebration Charades'. Teacher writes 'wedding', 'birthday', 'Eid', 'Green March' on slips. Students take turns acting out a celebration while others guess, saying 'Is it a birthday?'
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Celebration Bingo' - Students have cards with words like 'cake', 'gifts', 'music', 'family'. Teacher calls out words, students mark and shout 'Bingo!' when complete
Alternative 2: 'Quick Share' - Students turn to a partner and say 'My favorite celebration is... because...'
pres: Presentation: Show flashcards of celebration customs (cutting cake, dancing, gifts, praying). Model sentences: 'At a wedding, people dance.' 'On Eid, families visit each other.' Check understanding with thumbs up/down: 'Do people eat cake at Eid?'
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use a short story about a Moroccan wedding, highlighting customs like 'henna' and 'music'
Alternative 2: Bring in realia (a gift box, a small cake model) and describe each item's role in celebrations
prac: Guided practice: 'Match the Custom' worksheet. Students match pictures of celebrations to sentences (e.g., 'At a birthday party, people sing Happy Birthday'). In pairs, they practice saying the sentences with correct stress.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Sentence Auction' - Write correct and incorrect sentences on the board. Students 'buy' the correct ones with play money
Alternative 2: 'Chain Drill' - Teacher starts 'At a wedding...', next student adds 'and people dance', next adds 'and eat cake'
ls: Listening slot: Play a short audio of someone describing a Moroccan Independence Day celebration. Students listen and tick three customs they hear from a list (e.g., 'flags', 'parades', 'family meals')
re: Reactivation game: 'Stand Up, Sit Down'. Teacher says celebration words (e.g., 'gifts' - stand, 'prayer' - sit). Students move quickly to check recall of vocabulary.
prod: Production task: In teams of 3, students plan a 'Green March Celebration' for the American Space. They must decide: 1) What food? 2) What music? 3) What activity? Each team presents their plan using 'We will...' and 'People can...'
rw: Reading and writing slot: Students read a short text about a typical Moroccan wedding custom (e.g., 'henna night'). Then, they write 5 sentences for an invitation: 'You are invited to my wedding. It is on... We will... Please bring... Wear...'
st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Sing 'Happy Birthday' with actions. Close with: 'Today we learned to describe celebrations and write invitations. Thank you, class!'
g: Students draw a celebration custom (e.g., 'gifts') while others guess
Walk around asking 'Find someone who has been to a wedding. When?'
Teacher asks 'What do people eat at Eid?' Students race to answer 'couscous'
Match invitation phrases ('You are invited...') to celebration pictures
Students race to write 5 celebration words from memory on the board
diff: Fast finishers: Design a poster for their celebration with 3 customs and a date
Support learners: Use a sentence frame for writing: 'My celebration is on... We will... Please come...'
hw: Homework 1: Write 5 sentences about your favorite Moroccan celebration
Homework 2: Create an invitation to a family event using the phrases from class
Homework 3: Draw a picture of a celebration and label 3 customs
tip: Connect lessons to local culture by always including Moroccan celebrations (Eid, weddings, Green March) alongside Western ones. This builds relevance and respect for learners' backgrounds.
